title: Tanbeeh: Revolutionizing Safety and Efficiency with AI
summary: DP World reports that Tanbeeh reduced gate entry from three minutes to 15 seconds. The platform also monitors fire and protective equipment; prevented injuries are unproven.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: DP World reports that Tanbeeh reduced gate entry from three minutes to 15 seconds. The platform also monitors fire and protective equipment, but prevented injuries are unproven. The report alternates between PPE detection accuracy and compliance and gives inconsistent fire-detection times.
purpose: Automate industrial access control and safety monitoring.
location: DP World industrial facilities; particular site unspecified

ratings.reason: DP World reports that gate entry fell from three minutes to 15 seconds in live operations.
Greater worker safety is intended. Prevented injuries are unmeasured.
Lower congestion emissions and fewer harmful fires are intended, with no measured public outcome.

ai_role.statement: Computer vision supports gate authentication and safety monitoring. Faster gate processing is reported. Prevented injuries remain unproven.

evidence.citation: Project account in International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact, 2025. Information current as of June 2025. Outcomes are reported by the project team. The account provides no independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Use Case 1: Tanbeeh: Revolutionizing Safety and Efficiency with AI

produced_by: Conditions that could produce the benefit are unspecified.
must_hold: On-premises CCTV feeds and a high-bandwidth local network
Locally adapted vision models and operational staff

headline: Tanbeeh speeds gate entry at DP World
claim_basis: Sources: the makers' report. The cited evidence includes no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
